**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination / Technical and Vocational Education Examination. Subject: Religious Studies (code 0785), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Paper 2: The Old Testament/Jewish Bible and World Faiths. Duration: three hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR questions chosen from any ONE SECTION ONLY. All questions carry equal marks (25 marks each).

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Sections of the paper: 1.0 The Old Testament/Jewish Bible, Section 1.1 The Patriarchs to David (questions 1 to 6); Section 5.3 Islam (questions 7 to 12); Section 5.5 African Traditional Religious Beliefs and Practices (questions 13 to 18).
incertitudes: Question 11 : énoncé « Comment » (« Comment on the place of prophets in Islam ») ; points imprimés « (25 marks) ». Le nombre de prophètes nommés dans le Coran est donné comme « about twenty-five », valeur d'usage ; aucun autre chiffre.
Neutralité : les croyances sont présentées comme celles des musulmans (« Muslims believe », « according to Islamic tradition ») ; aucun numéro de sourate ni de hadith n'est cité.

Règle de choix : le sujet impose « Answer FOUR questions chosen from any ONE SECTION ONLY ». Cette règle (4 questions d'UNE SEULE section) n'est pas exprimable avec `parmi` (un seul groupe) ni `ou` (sous-questions) : `regles_choix` reste vide dans tous les fichiers et la consigne complète est recopiée dans `introduction_markdown`.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées de mémoire, sans accès à une source ; les références sont limitées à des passages et faits bien établis, les autres points sont formulés prudemment (« according to Islamic tradition », « Muslims believe »). À faire relire par un spécialiste des études religieuses avant mise en avant.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Comment on the place of prophets in Islam.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** In Islam, belief in prophets (anbiya') and messengers (rusul) is one of the six articles of faith. Muslims believe that God has sent prophets to every community to guide humankind, and that the last of them is Muhammad. The place of prophets is therefore central, though they are never worshipped.

**1. Prophets are an article of faith.** A Muslim must believe in all the prophets without distinction. The Qur'an says believers make no distinction between any of God's messengers. Denying one of them is regarded as a serious fault.

**2. Prophets carry God's revelation.** Muslims believe that prophets receive revelation from God and convey it to people: Musa (Moses) received the Tawrat, Dawud (David) the Zabur, Isa (Jesus) the Injil and Muhammad the Qur'an. About twenty-five prophets are named in the Qur'an, among them Adam, Nuh (Noah), Ibrahim (Abraham), Ismail, Ishaq, Yaqub, Yusuf (Joseph), Musa, Dawud, Sulayman (Solomon), Isa and Muhammad. Others are believed to have been sent whose names are not given.

**3. They all bring the same basic message.** Every prophet called people to worship the One God (tawhid), to avoid idolatry and to live righteously, and to prepare for the Day of Judgement. Differences concern details of law, not the core of faith. In this way Islam sees itself as the confirmation of the prophetic tradition, not as a new religion.

**4. They are models of conduct.** Prophets are believed to be protected from major sins and from error in conveying the message (ismah), and are examples of patience (Ayyub or Job), faith (Ibrahim), leadership (Musa) and compassion. The Prophet Muhammad's sayings and actions (Sunnah) form a source of guidance after the Qur'an.

**5. They are honoured but not divine.** Muslims say "peace be upon him" after the name of a prophet. Prophets are human beings: they eat, sleep, marry and die. Islam rejects any worship of prophets or the belief that any of them is divine. For example, Isa is honoured as a prophet, born of the virgin Maryam, and as the Messiah (al-Masih), but not as the Son of God.

**6. Some have special rank.** The Qur'an says that God favoured some prophets above others. Ibrahim is called the friend of God (Khalil), Musa the one who spoke with God (Kalim), Isa a word from God. The five "resolute" prophets (Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, Muhammad) are especially honoured.

**7. Muhammad is the last and universal prophet.** The Qur'an calls him the "Seal of the Prophets" (khatam an-nabiyyin): Muslims believe that no prophet will come after him and that his message is for all people and all times. Because of this he is the model for Muslims in worship, law, character and leadership of the community, and his name is joined to that of God in the declaration of faith.

**8. They serve as intercessors and witnesses.** Muslims believe that on the Day of Judgement, prophets will bear witness for or against their communities, and that the Prophet Muhammad will have a role of intercession, though only by God's permission.

**Conclusion.** Prophets hold a very high place in Islam as God's chosen messengers, bearers of revelation, models of conduct and witnesses on the Day of Judgement, while remaining human and never to be worshipped. Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets, holds the highest place because his message completes the earlier ones.
